claim: PRC1 plays essential roles in development and disease pathogenesis.
source: The Polycomb PRC1 plays essential roles in development and disease pathogenesis.
evidence: This is a statement in the abstract that is supported by citations in the introduction section.

claim: Targeting of PRC1 to chromatin is thought to be mediated by Cbx family proteins binding to H3K27me3.
source: Targeting of PRC1 to chromatin is thought to be mediated by the Cbx family proteins (Cbx2/4/6/7/8) binding to histone H3 with a K27me3 modification (H3K27me3).
evidence: This statement reflects the prevailing view in the field, supported by citations in the introduction.

claim: H3K27me3 contributes significantly to the targeting of Cbx7 and Cbx8 to chromatin.
source: H3K27me3 contributes significantly to the targeting of Cbx7 and Cbx8 to chromatin, but less to Cbx2, Cbx4, and Cbx6.
evidence: This claim is supported by live-cell SMT experiments in Eed−/− and Ezh2−/− mES cells showing reduced chromatin binding of Cbx7 and Cbx8.

claim: H3K27me3 plays a less important role in targeting Cbx2, Cbx4, and Cbx6 to chromatin.
source: H3K27me3 contributes significantly to the targeting of Cbx7 and Cbx8 to chromatin, but less to Cbx2, Cbx4, and Cbx6.
evidence: This is supported by SMT data showing similar chromatin-bound levels of Cbx2, Cbx4, and Cbx6 in wild-type and Eed−/− or Ezh2−/− mES cells.

claim: Genetic disruption of PRC1 complex formation facilitates the targeting of Cbx7 to chromatin.
source: Genetic disruption of the complex formation of PRC1 facilitates the targeting of Cbx7 to chromatin.
evidence: This is supported by SMT experiments showing increased chromatin-bound fraction of Cbx7 in Ring1a−/−/Ring1b−/− and Bmi1−/−/Mel18−/− mES cells.

claim: The CD and AT-hook-like (ATL) motif of Cbx7 constitute a functional DNA-binding unit.
source: Biochemical analyses uncover that the CD and AT-hook-like (ATL) motif of Cbx7 constitute a functional DNA-binding unit.
evidence: This is supported by EMSA experiments showing that CD-ATLCbx7 binds DNA while CDCbx7 or ATLCbx7 alone do not.

claim: Cbx7 is targeted to chromatin by co-recognition of H3K27me3 and DNA.
source: Live-cell SMT of Cbx7 mutants demonstrates that Cbx7 is targeted to chromatin by co-recognizing of H3K27me3 and DNA.
evidence: This is supported by SMT experiments with Cbx7 mutants lacking CD or ATL showing reduced chromatin binding.

claim: PcG proteins function as histone-modifying enzymes and regulate gene expression via modulating higher order chromatin structures.
source: This is exemplified by Polycomb group (PcG) proteins that function as histone-modifying enzymes and regulate gene expression via modulating higher order chromatin structures (Simon and Kingston, 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Simon and Kingston, 2013.

claim: PcG proteins were initially identified as regulators of body structure specification in Drosophila.
source: PcG proteins were initially identified as a body structure specification in Drosophila (Lewis, 1978).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Lewis, 1978.

claim: In mammals, PcG orthologs are essential for normal embryonic development and disease pathogenesis.
source: In mammals, PcG orthologs are essential for normal embryonic development and disease pathogenesis (Helin and Dhanak, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Helin and Dhanak, 2013.

claim: PcG subunits are frequently overexpressed or mutated in cancer.
source: For example, PcG subunits are frequently overexpressed or mutated in cancer, and perturbing PcG interactions can suppress cancer growth (Helin and Dhanak, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Helin and Dhanak, 2013.

claim: Perturbing PcG interactions can suppress cancer growth.
source: For example, PcG subunits are frequently overexpressed or mutated in cancer, and perturbing PcG interactions can suppress cancer growth (Helin and Dhanak, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Helin and Dhanak, 2013.

claim: PRC2 catalyzes di- and tri-methylation of lysine 27 on histone H3 (H3K27me2/3) by the SET domain of Ezh2 (or Ezh1).
source: PRC2 is a methyltransferase that catalyzes di- and tri-methylation of lysine 27 on histone H3 (H3K27me2/3) by the SET domain of Ezh2 (or Ezh1) (Cao et al., 2002; Czermin et al., 2002; Kuzmichev et al., 2002; Margueron et al., 2008; Muller et al., 2002; Shen et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Ezh2 requires Suz12 and Eed for enzymatic activity.
source: Unlike most SET domain methyltransferases, Ezh2 requires Suz12 and Eed for enzymatic activity (Cao and Zhang, 2004; Martin et al., 2006; Montgomery et al., 2005; Pasini et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Rbbp4 and Rbbp7 are stoichiometric subunits of PRC2.
source: Additionally, Rbbp4 and Rbbp7 are stoichiometric subunits of PRC2 (Cao et al., 2002; Cao and Zhang, 2004; Margueron and Reinberg, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: PRC1 is an ubiquitin ligase that monoubiquitylates histone H2A on lysine 119 (H2AK119ub1).
source: In contrast, PRC1 is an ubiquitin ligase that monoubiquitylates histone H2A on lysine 119 (H2AK119ub1) (de Napoles et al., 2004; Wang et al., 2004a).
evidence: This is supported by citations.

claim: PRC1 complexes form around Ring1b (or Ring1a) subunits with which one of the six Pcgf proteins (Pcgf1-6) associates.
source: PRC1 complexes form around Ring1b (or Ring1a) subunits with which one of the six Pcgf proteins (Pcgf1-6) associates (Gao et al., 2012; Gil and O'Loghlen, 2014; Tavares et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: The Ring-Pcgf2 (Mel18) or Pcgf4 (Bmi1) heterodimers are incorporated in canonical PRC1 (Cbx-PRC1).
source: The Ring-Pcgf2 (Mel18) or Pcgf4 (Bmi1) heterodimers are incorporated in canonical PRC1 (Cbx-PRC1; the functional homolog to Drosophila PRC1) and the other Ring-Pcgf heterodimers are assembled in variant PRC1 (vPRC1).
evidence: This is a statement about PRC1 complex composition.

claim: The Cbx-PRC1 complex is composed of one of each of four different core subunits: Ring1, Pcgf, Phc, and Cbx.
source: The Cbx-PRC1 complex is composed of one of each of four different core subunits, Ring1 (Ring1a/Ring1b), Pcgf (Mel18/Bmi1), Phc (Phc1/2/3), and Cbx (Cbx2/4/6/7/8).
evidence: This describes the composition of Cbx-PRC1.

claim: The vPRC1 complexes contain Rybp or Yaf instead of Cbx and Phc.
source: In contrast, the vPRC1 complexes contain Rybp or Yaf instead of Cbx and Phc.
evidence: This describes the composition of vPRC1.

claim: dPRC2 is recruited to Polycomb response elements (PRE) by its interaction with sequence-specific DNA-binding proteins.
source: dPRC2 is recruited to Polycomb response elements (PRE) by its interaction with sequence-specific DNA-binding proteins and then modifies chromatin with H3K27me3 that recruits dPRC1.
evidence: This describes the recruitment mechanism in Drosophila.

claim: dPRC1 is displaced from chromatin in dPRC2 mutants.
source: Consistent with the notion, genetic analyses have demonstrated that dPRC1 and dPRC2 co-regulate PcG target genes and dPRC1 is displaced from chromatin in dPRC2 mutants (Cao et al., 2002; Wang et al., 2004b).
evidence: This is supported by citations to genetic analyses.

claim: dPRC1 and dPRC2 co-occupy many PcG target genes.
source: Genome-wide studies have shown that dPRC1 and dPRC2 co-occupy many PcG target genes (Schwartz et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citation to genome-wide studies.

claim: The recruitment of mammalian PRC1 has been broadly defined as H3K27me3-dependent and –independent recruitment mechanisms.
source: In mammals, the recruitment of PRC1 is enigmatic and complicated, and has been broadly defined as H3K27me3-dependent and –independent recruitment mechanisms (Blackledge et al., 2015; Farcas et al., 2012; He et al., 2013; Tavares et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: PRC1, in some cases, recruits PRC2.
source: An additional layer of complexity is added when considering that PRC1, in some cases, recruits PRC2 (Blackledge et al., 2014; Cooper et al., 2014; Kalb et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: The Cbx family members and dPc both contain a conserved chromodomain (CD).
source: The H3K27me3-dependent recruitment of mammalian PRC1 originates from the Drosophila model and is based on the facts that the Cbx family members and dPc both contain a conserved chromodomain (CD) (Blackledge et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation and is a structural fact.

claim: The Cbx CDs have a much weaker affinity for H3K27me3 compared to the dPc CD.
source: First, unlike to the dPc CD, the Cbx CDs have a much weaker affinity for H3K27me3 (Bernstein et al., 2006; Kaustov et al., 2011; Tardat et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to biochemical studies.

claim: The Cbx2 CD shows preference for H3K27me3.
source: The Cbx2 CD shows preference for H3K27me3 while the Cbx4 and Cbx7 CDs exhibit preference for H3K9me3 (Bernstein et al., 2006; Kaustov et al., 2011; Tardat et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to biochemical studies.

claim: The Cbx4 and Cbx7 CDs exhibit preference for H3K9me3.
source: The Cbx2 CD shows preference for H3K27me3 while the Cbx4 and Cbx7 CDs exhibit preference for H3K9me3 (Bernstein et al., 2006; Kaustov et al., 2011; Tardat et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to biochemical studies.

claim: The affinity of the Cbx6 and Cbx8 CDs for H3K27me3 is nearly undetectable.
source: The affinity of the Cbx6 and Cbx8 CDs for H3K27me3 is nearly undetectable (Bernstein et al., 2006; Kaustov et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to biochemical studies.

claim: H3K27me3 forms a broad domain and the binding PRC1 is sharply localized within the H3K27me3 domain.
source: Likewise, genome-wide approaches have demonstrated that H3K27me3 forms a broad domain and the binding PRC1 is sharply localized within the H3K27me3 domain, and that a subset of H3K27me3 domains corresponds to PRC1 binding sites (Ku et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to genome-wide studies.

claim: A subset of H3K27me3 domains corresponds to PRC1 binding sites.
source: Likewise, genome-wide approaches have demonstrated that H3K27me3 forms a broad domain and the binding PRC1 is sharply localized within the H3K27me3 domain, and that a subset of H3K27me3 domains corresponds to PRC1 binding sites (Ku et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to genome-wide studies.

claim: HaloTag was fused at the N-terminus of Cbx proteins under an inducible, tetracycline response element (TRE)-tight promoter.
source: HaloTag was fused at the N-terminus of Cbx proteins under an inducible, tetracycline response element (TRE)-tight promoter (Figure 1A).
evidence: This describes the experimental design shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The fusion genes were stably integrated into the genome of wild-type (PGK12.1) mES cells.
source: These fusion genes were stably integrated into the genome of wild-type (PGK12.1) mES cells.
evidence: This describes the experimental method.

claim: Highly inclined thin illumination (HILO) was used to avoid stray-light reflection and to reduce background from cell auto-fluorescence.
source: We used highly inclined thin illumination (HILO) to avoid stray-light reflection and to reduce background from cell auto-fluorescence (Tokunaga et al., 2008) (Figure 1B).
evidence: This describes the imaging method with citation and reference to Figure 1B.

claim: The HaloTag ligand of the bright, photostable fluorophore Janelia Fluor 549 (JF549) allowed for visualization of single HaloTag-Cbx molecules at their basal expression level without doxycycline induction.
source: The HaloTag ligand of the bright, photostable fluorophore Janelia Fluor 549 (JF549) allowed for visualization of single HaloTag-Cbx molecules at their basal expression level without doxycycline induction (Grimm et al., 2015) (Figure 1C).
evidence: This describes the labeling method with citation and reference to Figure 1C.

claim: The majority of H2A-HaloTag molecules were stationary while almost every HaloTag-NLS molecules were mobile.
source: A visual inspection of single-molecule imaging tracks showed HaloTag-NLS and H2A-HaloTag exhibited obvious differences (Video 1 and 2). The majority of H2A-HaloTag molecules were stationary while almost every HaloTag-NLS molecules were mobile.
evidence: This is based on visual inspection of single-molecule tracks shown in Videos 1 and 2.

claim: ∼15–35% of the tracks have a frame number ≤ 3.
source: Analysis of the distributions of track length for HaloTag labelled molecules indicated that ∼15–35% of the tracks have a frame number ≤ 3 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is based on analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

source: We measured F1 = (72 ± 1)% (Dm1= 0.032 ± 0.001 µm2s-1), F2 = (14 ± 2)% (Dm2= 0.50 ± 0.06 µm2s-1), and F3 = (14 ± 2)% (Dm3= 2.4 ± 0.2 µm2s-1) (Figure 1F and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from SMT data shown in Figure 1F.

source: We measured F2 = (71 ± 1)% (Dm2= 0.24 ± 0.03 µm2s-1) and F3 = (29 ± 2)% (Dm3= 2.5 ± 0.1 µm2s-1) (Figure 1F and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from SMT data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: The CB population of HaloTag-NLS is almost undetectable.
source: Experimental evidence supports the assignment of the F1 component as the CB population because (1) the CB population of HaloTag-NLS is almost undetectable
evidence: This is based on the fitting results showing no F1 component for HaloTag-NLS.

claim: ∼70% of H2A-HaloTag molecules are incorporated into chromatin.
source: (2) ∼70% of H2A-HaloTag molecules are incorporated into chromatin, which is consistent with the reported results from fluorescence photobleaching after recovery (Ren et al., 2008)
evidence: This is based on SMT data and is consistent with previous FRAP studies.

claim: The diffusion constant and fractional size of the CB population of H2A-HaloTag agree with recent single-molecule reports.
source: and (3) the diffusion constant and fractional size of the CB population of H2A-HaloTag agree with recent single-molecule reports (Gebhardt et al., 2013; Mazza et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by comparison with cited single-molecule studies.

source: We measured F1 = (30 ± 1)%, F2 = (61 ± 1)%, and F3 = (9 ± 4)% for HaloTag-Cbx2
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from SMT data.
This is a quantitative measurement from SMT data.
This is a quantitative measurement from SMT data.
This is a quantitative measurement from SMT data.

source: and F1 = (26 ± 1)%, F2 = (50 ± 2)%, and F3 = (24 ± 4)% for HaloTag-Cbx8 (Figure 1F and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from SMT data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: The Cbx proteins exhibit distinct chromatin-associating capacities.
source: These data provided a few novel observations: (1) the Cbx proteins exhibit distinct chromatin-associating capacities
evidence: This is inferred from the different F1 values measured for different Cbx proteins.

claim: Cbx2, Cbx7, and Cbx8 exhibit the highest chromatin-bound level while Cbx4 has the lowest one.
source: (2) Cbx2, Cbx7, and Cbx8 exhibit the highest chromatin-bound level while Cbx4 has the lowest one
evidence: This is based on comparison of F1 values across Cbx proteins.

claim: The fractional sizes of the FD components are distinct among the Cbx family proteins.
source: (3) the fractional sizes of the FD components are distinct among the Cbx family proteins
evidence: This is based on comparison of F3 values across Cbx proteins.

claim: Except for Cbx2, the fractional sizes of the ID components are similar among the Cbx proteins.
source: (4) except for Cbx2, the fractional sizes of the ID components are similar among the Cbx proteins
evidence: This is based on comparison of F2 values across Cbx proteins.

claim: Among the Cbx proteins, the diffusion constants are distinct for the ID components, but similar for the FD components.
source: and (5) among the Cbx proteins, the diffusion constants are distinct for the ID components, but similar for the FD components.
evidence: This is based on comparison of Dm2 and Dm3 values across Cbx proteins.

claim: The Cbx proteins employ distinct ways to interact with chromatin and to explore the nucleus.
source: Altogether, our results demonstrate that the Cbx proteins employ distinct ways to interact with chromatin and to explore the nucleus.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the distinct diffusion and binding properties measured for different Cbx proteins.

claim: Cbx7 and Cbx8 are displaced from chromatin in Eed−/− and Ezh2−/− mES cells.
source: At the single-molecule sensitivity, we demonstrated that Cbx7 and Cbx8 are displaced from chromatin in Eed−/− and Ezh2−/− mES cells.
evidence: This is based on SMT data showing reduced or undetectable CB fractions in these knockout cells.

claim: The introduction of Eed into Eed−/− mES cells and of Ezh2 into Ezh2−/− mES cells restored the Cbx7 and Cbx8 association with chromatin and the H3K27me3 level.
source: The introduction of Eed into Eed−/− mES cells and of Ezh2 into Ezh2−/− mES cells restored the Cbx7 and Cbx8 association with chromatin and the H3K27me3 level.
evidence: This is based on SMT and immunofluorescence data showing rescue of chromatin binding and H3K27me3 levels.

claim: H3K27me3 directly controls the association of Cbx7 and Cbx8 with chromatin.
source: Thus, it is likely that H3K27me3 directly controls the association of Cbx7 and Cbx8 with chromatin.
evidence: This is inferred from the loss and rescue experiments.

claim: Cbx7 is displaced from chromatin in Eed−/− mES cells according to previous genome-wide ChIP-Seq analysis.
source: Consistent with this notion, previous genome-wide ChIP-Seq analysis demonstrated that Cbx7 is displaced from chromatin in Eed−/− mES cells (Morey et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a ChIP-Seq study.

claim: The removal of H3K27me3 has no or small effects on the association of Cbx2, Cbx4, and Cbx6 with chromatin.
source: We found that the removal of H3K27me3 has no or small effects on the association of Cbx2, Cbx4, and Cbx6 with chromatin.
evidence: This is based on SMT data showing similar CB fractions in wild-type and Eed−/− or Ezh2−/− cells for these proteins.

claim: Cbx6 does not interact with Ring1b.
source: No effects on the Cbx6 association with chromatin is consistent with previous studies where Cbx6 does not interact with Ring1b and only 5% of Cbx6 target genes are occupied by H3K27me3 in mES cells (Morey et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Morey et al., 2012.

claim: Only 5% of Cbx6 target genes are occupied by H3K27me3 in mES cells.
source: No effects on the Cbx6 association with chromatin is consistent with previous studies where Cbx6 does not interact with Ring1b and only 5% of Cbx6 target genes are occupied by H3K27me3 in mES cells (Morey et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Morey et al., 2012.

claim: Cbx2 and Cbx4 form the Cbx-PRC1 complex and overlap with H3K27me3 Polycomb domains.
source: In contrast to Cbx6, Cbx2 and Cbx4 form the Cbx-PRC1 complex and overlap with H3K27me3 Polycomb domains (Gao et al., 2012; Mardaryev et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations.

claim: Cbx4 is a SUMO E3 ligase and can function in an H3K27me3-dependent or –independent way.
source: Cbx4 is a SUMO E3 ligase and can function as the H3K27me3-dependent or –independent way (Kagey et al., 2003; Li et al., 2014; Mardaryev et al., 2016; Roscic et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Cbx2 is targeted to mitotic chromosomes independently of PRC1 and PRC2, and directly recruits the canonical PRC1 components to mitotic chromosomes.
source: Our recent study has shown that Cbx2 is targeted to mitotic chromosomes independently of PRC1 and PRC2, and directly recruits the canonical PRC1 components to mitotic chromosomes (Zhen et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to the authors' previous study.

claim: Cbx2 targets the canonical PRC1 to constitutive heterochromatin by directly recognizing pericentromeric chromatin during early mouse development.
source: Another study has demonstrated that Cbx2 targets the canonical PRC1 to constitutive heterochromatin by directly recognizing pericentromeric chromatin during early mouse development (Tardat et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation.

claim: Cbx2 can directly bind to and compact reconstituted nucleosomes in vitro.
source: Additionally, in vitro study has shown that Cbx2 can directly bind to and compact reconstituted nucleosomes (Grau et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to an in vitro study.

claim: Additional mechanisms exist to target Cbx2, Cbx4, and Cbx6 to chromatin.
source: Thus, these studies suggest additional mechanisms exist to target Cbx2, Cbx4, and Cbx6 to chromatin.
evidence: This is inferred from the cited studies and the SMT data showing H3K27me3-independent chromatin binding.

claim: The level of CDCbx7 at chromatin is less than 30% of Cbx7.
source: We observed that the level of CDCbx7 at chromatin is less than 30% of Cbx7
evidence: This is based on comparison of F1 values for HaloTag-CDCbx7 and HaloTag-Cbx7.

claim: The residence time of the stable chromatin-bound population of CDCbx7 is about 65% of Cbx7.
source: and that the residence time of the stable chromatin-bound population of CDCbx7 is about 65% of Cbx7.
evidence: This is based on comparison of τsb values for HaloTag-CDCbx7 and HaloTag-Cbx7.

claim: Cbx7F11A and Cbx7△CD both remain associating with chromatin.
source: Mutational analysis demonstrated that Cbx7F11A and Cbx7△CD both remain associating with chromatin.
evidence: This is based on SMT data showing detectable CB fractions for these mutants.

claim: Additional factor(s) exist(s) to target the Cbx7 protein to chromatin.
source: These data imply that additional factor(s) exist(s) to target the Cbx7 protein to chromatin.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that CD-deficient mutants still bind chromatin.

claim: CDCbx7 and ATLCbx7 do not bind to DNA individually.
source: Consistent with previous reports, our data showed that CDCbx7 and ATLCbx7 do not bind to DNA, respectively (Bernstein et al., 2006; Reeves and Nissen, 1990).
evidence: This is based on EMSA data and is consistent with cited studies.

claim: CDCbx7 and ATLCbx7 together function as a DNA-binding unit.
source: Interestingly, our results demonstrated that CDCbx7 and ATLCbx7 together function as a DNA-binding unit.
evidence: This is based on EMSA data showing that CD-ATLCbx7 binds DNA.

claim: CD-ATLCbx7 exhibited much higher affinity for dsDNA than for ssDNA, dsRNA, and ssRNA.
source: CD-ATLCbx7 exhibited much higher affinity for dsDNA than for ssDNA, dsRNA, and ssRNA.
evidence: This is based on competitive EMSA experiments.

claim: Perturbation of the DNA-binding capacity of CD-ATLCbx7 impaired the level of Cbx7 at chromatin and reduced the Cbx7 residence time.
source: Perturbation of the DNA-binding capacity of CD-ATLCbx7 impaired the level of Cbx7 at chromatin and reduced the Cbx7 residence time.
evidence: This is based on SMT data for Cbx7 mutants with disrupted ATL.

claim: Deletion of both CDCbx7 and ATLCbx7 results in the significantly reduced level of the stable chromatin-bound population.
source: Deletion of both CDCbx7 and ATL Cbx7 results in the significantly reduced level of the stable chromatin-bound population.
evidence: This is based on SMT data for HaloTag-Cbx7△CD-ATL.

claim: The co-recognition of H3K27me3 and DNA by the CD-ATLCbx7 module contributes significantly to the targeting of Cbx7 to chromatin.
source: Thus, our data demonstrate that the co-recognition of H3K27me3 and DNA by the CD-ATLCbx7 module contributes significantly to the targeting of Cbx7 to chromatin.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined SMT and biochemical data.

claim: Mel18 binds DNA directly in vitro.
source: Given that previous studies have shown that Mel18 binds DNA directly in vitro (Akasaka et al., 1996)
evidence: This is supported by citation.

claim: The Ring1b-Mel18 ubiquitin module recognizes reconstituted nucleosome.
source: and the Ring1b-Mel18 ubiquitin module recognizes reconstituted nucleosome (McGinty et al., 2014)
evidence: This is supported by citation.

claim: Depletion of Ring1a/Ring1b and Bmi1/Mel18 results in the increased chromatin-bound levels and the increased residence times of Cbx7.
source: Interestingly, our single-molecule approaches demonstrated that depletion of Ring1a/Ring1b and Bmi1/Mel18 results in the increased chromatin-bound levels and the increased residence times of Cbx7.
evidence: This is based on SMT data in knockout cells.

claim: SWR1 is recruited to promoter regions containing nucleosome free region > 50 bp and an adjoining nucleosome by the nanomolar DNA-binding affinity of Swc2.
source: For example, SWR1 is recruited to promoter regions containing nucleosome free region > 50 bp and an adjoining nucleosome by the nanomolar DNA-binding affinity of Swc2, a subunit of SWR1.
evidence: This is an example from the literature cited to support the concept of hierarchical cooperation.

claim: The micromolar affinity of Bdf1 bromodomains for acetylated histones directs SWR1 binding to the +1 nucleosome over the -1 nucleosome.
source: Once bound, the micromolar affinity of Bdf1 bromodomains for acetylated histones directs SWR1 binding to the +1 nucleosome over the -1 nucleosome (Ranjan et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation.

claim: Hierarchical cooperation between DNA and histone modifications could underpin the SWR1's role in promoting H2A.Z replacement.
source: Thus, hierarchical cooperation between DNA and histone modifications could underpin the SWR1's role in promoting H2A.Z replacement.
evidence: This is inferred from the cited study on SWR1.

claim: The Rpd3S histone deacetylase complex binds to H3K36-methylated dinucleosome with 100 pM affinity by multiple engagements of histone modifications and DNA.
source: Another example is that the Rpd3S histone deacetylase complex binds to H3K36-methylated dinucleosome with 100 pM affinity by multiple engagements of histone modifications and DNA (Huh et al., 2012; Li et al., 2007b).
evidence: This is supported by citations.

claim: The DNA- and histone-binding abilities of Eaf3 are self-contained and allosterically regulated by Rco1.
source: The DNA- and histone-binding abilities of Eaf3, a subunit of Rpd3S, are self-contained and allosterically regulated by Rco1, another subunit of Rpd3S (Ruan et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation.

claim: The mechanism of targeting of Cbx7 to chromatin is dependent on hierarchical cooperation via co-recognition of DNA and H3K27me3 by the CD-ATLCbx7 entity.
source: Our results suggest that the mechanism of targeting of Cbx7 to chromatin is dependent on hierarchical cooperation via co-recognition of DNA and H3K27me3 by the CD-ATLCbx7 entity (Figure 8).
evidence: This is a model proposed based on the experimental data, illustrated in Figure 8.

claim: Cbx7-PRC1 is recruited to chromatin by the CDCbx7 recognition of H3K27me3.
source: We propose that Cbx7-PRC1 is recruited to chromatin by the CDCbx7 recognition of H3K27me3.
evidence: This is part of the proposed model.

claim: The interaction between H3K27me3 and CDCbx7 triggers conformational changes of the Cbx7-PRC1 complex, which drive the high-affinity interaction between DNA and CD-ATLCbx7.
source: We hypothesize that the interaction between H3K27me3 and CDCbx7 triggers conformational changes of the Cbx7-PRC1 complex, which drive the high-affinity interaction between DNA and CD-ATLCbx7.
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed by the authors.

claim: The binding of CD-ATLCbx7 to DNA is auto-inhibited by unknown mechanisms and allosterically regulated by the CDCbx7 interaction with H3K27me3.
source: Implicit in this model is that the binding of CD-ATLCbx7 to DNA is auto-inhibited by unknown mechanisms and allosterically regulated by the CDCbx7 interaction with H3K27me3.
evidence: This is a speculation implicit in the proposed model.

claim: H3K27me3 allosterically activates the methyltransferase activity of the PRC2 complex by its interaction with the C-terminus of Eed.
source: Previous studies have shown that H3K27me3 allosterically activates the methyltransferase activity of the PRC2 complex by its interaction with the C-terminus of Eed (Jiao and Liu, 2015; Margueron et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations.

claim: The allosteric activation facilitates the progression of the H3K27me3 mark on chromatin.
source: The allosteric activation facilitates the progression of the H3K27me3 mark on chromatin.
evidence: This is inferred from the cited studies on PRC2 allosteric regulation.

claim: H3K27me3 was almost undetectable in Eed−/− mES cells.
source: H3K27me3 was almost undetectable in Eed−/− mES cells (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is shown by immunofluorescence in Figure 2E.

claim: The level of H3K27m3 was greatly reduced in Ezh2−/−mES cells in comparison with wild-type mES cells.
source: The level of H3K27m3 was greatly reduced in Ezh2−/−mES cells in comparison with wild-type mES cells (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is shown by immunofluorescence in Figure 2E.

claim: The residual level of H3K27me3 in Ezh2−/− cells was most likely contributed by Ezh1.
source: The residual level of H3K27me3 was most likely contributed by Ezh1 (Margueron et al., 2008; Shen et al., 2008).
